relevance_note: The paper reports one person with a germline TNFAIP3 variant and an HA20 diagnosis, 'the genetic diagnosis of A20 haploinsufficiency was established', and describes her relatives individually.
method_note: Case report; no script transcribed any table (the paper has no data tables, only figures), so every span was copied by hand from the Markdown and each was checked verbatim against the file. In-scope people: the index patient, her father and her father's brother (both stated to carry the TNFAIP3 variant), her mother (stated to have been screened for TNFAIP3 mutations), and three untested paternal relatives the paper describes with individual-level clinical facts (paternal grandfather, brother of paternal grandfather, father's uncle); the last three get no variants row because the paper does not say they carry the variant. The paternal relatives are all described in the single sentence of the family history, so their spans overlap. Figure 9 (family tree) is an image and was not read; the label 'proband'/'index case' is not printed for the patient ('our patient', 'the index patient'), so she is labelled by rule 5 ('patient') and marked is_proband true because she is the single patient of this case report. Inheritance: for the patient and the father the paper states 'the paternal origin of the TNFAIP3 variant' and 'The same TNFAIP3 variant was also found in her father', so inheritance 'inherited paternal'; for the uncle the paper says only that he carries the variant. The TNFAIP3 variant is not described as de novo and no parental testing negatives are given. The girl's variant was shown by a custom gene panel (IUIS genes), so clinical_diagnosis_basis mentions both genetic testing and clinical features. Uncertainties recorded honestly as 'not reported': no cohort_size (single case report), the study's n_patients_reported set to 1 (the authors describe one patient with a TNFAIP3 variant first-hand; the father and uncle are relatives with the variant). The statement 'The other family members in the paternal line presented potential clinical conditions of HA20 but could not be screened for mutations' was NOT used to exclude any specific feature, because it names no feature. The girl's 'colonic lymphoid nodular hyperplasia' was entered in phenotypic_features but was not mapped onto the checklist item 'lymphoproliferation or lymphadenopathy' (it is mucosal lymphoid hyperplasia, not lymphadenopathy). 'vitiligo' and 'panniculitis' were mapped onto the checklist item 'skin lesions (rash, folliculitis, erythema nodosum)' although they are not among the examples printed in that item; this is flagged here. Steroid side effects are printed as 'weight gain, changes in mood and behaviour, diabetes.' - this steroid-induced diabetes was not counted as the checklist item 'type 1 diabetes'. Time course for inflammatory markers in the girl is not a contradiction: 'Blood tests showed a rise in inflammation indexes' at admission and later 'blood tests known as inflammatory markers were negative' after treatment; the checklist item is recorded as observed and both phenotypic_features rows are kept. A 'rise in inflammation indexes' row could not carry the CRP value as a span because the character before the unit 'mg/dl' in the file is not a plain space; the shorter span 'Blood tests showed a rise in inflammation indexes' is quoted instead. Normal general examinations and negative infection/neoplasia work-ups ('normal cardiovascular, thoracic and abdominal physical examination', 'exams for infectious disease and neoplastic conditions were all negative') are not entered as features, as they name no specific abnormality.

treatment_summary.value: intravenous steroid therapy (methylprednisolone 2 mg/kg daily); oral steroid therapy (betamethasone 0.2 mg/kg daily); oral iron supplementation; systemic corticosteroids (betamethasone 0.1 mg/kg) and IL1 receptor antagonist (Anakinra from 2 to 6 mg/kg); anti-TNF drug (Infliximab from 5 to 10 mg/kg) with Methotrexate (7 mg once a week); Adalimumab (20 mg/kg every two weeks) with Methotrexate; steroid therapy stopped because of side effects
span: Since the genetic definition was not available, during the initial hospitalization we started only intravenous steroid therapy (methylprednisolone 2 mg/kg daily).
At discharge, we continued an oral steroid therapy (betamethasone 0.2 mg/kg daily) without other immunosuppressive agents.
Moreover, in consideration of the low values of hemoglobin, she started an oral iron supplementation therapy and a gastroenterological follow-up was scheduled.
Initially, our patient was treated with a combination protocol, including systemic corticosteroids (betamethasone 0.1 mg/kg) and IL1 receptor antagonist (Anakinra from 2 to 6 mg/kg).
we shifted to an anti-TNF drug (Infliximab from 5 to 10 mg/kg, initially once a week and later every six weeks) in association with Methotrexate (7 mg once a week)
